summary: Separate indivisible updates from visibility and ordering so shared state has a defensible correctness argument.
outcomes: Explain an atomic read-modify-write and its contention cost.
State the scope and ordering needed for a producer–consumer handoff.
sequence: Interleave two updates and expose the lost-update case.
Replace the update with a scoped atomic operation.
Separate atomicity from ordering of other memory accesses.
Build a small release/acquire publication example.
Compare scopes and discuss when a different algorithm avoids contention.

visual.question: Does observing this flag guarantee that the data is ready?
visual.interaction: Step producer and consumer operations; compare a missing and a valid ordering edge.
